question: We need to log into a supplier portal nobody gives us an API for, click through it and pull a table, on a schedule and from a server. Running headless Chrome ourselves keeps breaking. Which service would you use for that, and what else did you look at before picking it?
summary: Test a portal table extraction and an expired-session retry. The recorded mentions do not show whether an agent can complete these tasks.

items.title: Test the documented integration
items.finding: JavaScript scenarios and cookies provide a documented route. Missing entry/OAuth/spec probes and unobserved account signup or key creation do not establish a failed extraction. Test this route with an authorized fixture before deciding whether its interaction model fits the real portal.
items.nextStep: Call the API from Node with a JavaScript scenario that logs into a controlled fixture portal and extracts a known table. Run the same job again with an expired test cookie. Detect the login page, refresh access through the supported flow and check that output contains the expected rows.
items.validation: Record scenario steps, response status and exact extracted rows. The scheduler and session renewal belong to the fixture; do not label an empty response a successful scrape.

sources.note: API key, cookies, JavaScript scenarios and extraction rules.

items.title: Make the relevant entry cost easy to check
items.finding: The pricing description contains no amount or entry condition. That metadata observation does not explain recommendation frequency.
items.nextStep: Check the current plan for this task before adding a concrete entry condition to the description. Keep paid features and hosted versus local costs distinct.
items.validation: Any proposed wording must match the chosen plan. No recommendation uplift has been measured.
